# Output dictionary

<!-- generated by tools/generate_features_md.py from politeness_py.feature_dictionary(); do not edit -->

What every value returned by `politeness-py` means. The same information is
available in code: `politeness_py.feature_dictionary()` (and
`feature_dictionary("dnm")`), and `politeness_py.describe(df)` summarises a
result table. Feature definitions come from the R package
[politeness](https://github.com/myeomans/politeness) (Yeomans, Kantor & Tingley).

## 1. `politeness()` columns

One row per input text, one column per feature. Cell values:

| `metric=` | value |
|---|---|
| `"count"` (default) | number of times the feature occurs in the text (integer ≥ 0) |
| `"binary"` | 1 if the feature occurs at least once, else 0 |
| `"average"` | occurrences per 100 words (`count * 100 / number of words`); `NaN` for a text without letters |

`parser="none"` returns the 33 columns available without part-of-speech
tagging; `parser="spacy"` returns 42 (it drops `Questions` and adds the
parse-based features). `drop_blank=True` removes columns that are 0 for every
text. *Availability*: **both** = same rule with either parser; **both (rule
differs)** = present in both, more precise with spaCy (e.g. negation-aware);
**spacy only** / **none only**.

| # | column | category | availability | meaning | how it is counted (parser="none") | how it is counted (parser="spacy") | example |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `Hedges` | Hedging & certainty | both | Indicators of uncertainty (hedging) | words from a 72-word hedge list (almost, apparently, maybe, might, perhaps, possibly, probably, seems, somewhat, suggest, ...) | same | "I might take the deal" |
| 2 | `Impersonal.Pronoun` | Pronouns & address | both | Non-person referents (it, that, this, something, ...) | quanteda dictionary 'Pronouns' (46 glob entries) | same | "That is a deal" |
| 3 | `Swearing` | Lexical | both | Vulgarity of all sorts | quanteda dictionary 'Swearing' (32 glob entries) | same | "The damn price is too high" |
| 4 | `Negation` | Lexical | both | Contradiction / negation words (not, no, never, nothing, cannot, ...) | quanteda dictionary 'Negation' (57 entries; contractions are expanded first, so don't -> do not) | same | "This cannot be your best offer" |
| 5 | `Filler.Pause` | Lexical | both | Filler words and verbal pauses | dictionary: er, sigh, hm*, uh*, um* | same | "That would be, um, fine" |
| 6 | `Informal.Title` | Pronouns & address | both | Informal forms of address | dictionary: dude*, bro*, boss, bud, buddy, champ, man, guy*, brotha, sista, son, sonny, chief | same | "Dude, that is quite an offer." |
| 7 | `Formal.Title` | Pronouns & address | both | Formal forms of address | dictionary: sir, ma'am, maam, mister, mr*, ms*, madam, miss, gentleman, lady | same | "Sir, that is quite an offer." |
| 8 | `Could.You` | Requests & agency | both | Indirect (counterfactual) request | phrases: could you / would you / might you | same | "Could you lower the price?" |
| 9 | `Can.You` | Requests & agency | both | Direct (indicative) request | phrases: can you / will you | same | "Can you lower the price?" |
| 10 | `By.The.Way` | Discourse markers | both | 'by the way' (indirect start) | phrase: by the way | same | "By the way, my old offer stands" |
| 11 | `Let.Me.Know` | Requests & agency | both | 'let me know' | phrase: let me know | same | "Let me know if that works" |
| 12 | `Goodbye` | Greetings & closings | both | Closings | phrases: goodbye / bye / see you later | same | "That's my best offer. Bye!" |
| 13 | `For.Me` | Requests & agency | both | Benefit for the speaker | phrases: ' for me ' / 'for us ' | same | "It would be great for me" |
| 14 | `For.You` | Requests & agency | both | Benefit for the addressee | phrase: ' for you ' | same | "It would be great for you" |
| 15 | `Reasoning` | Discourse markers | both | Explicit reference to reasons | substrings: reason, why i, why we, explain, caused, because | same | "I want to explain my offer price" |
| 16 | `Contrast.Conjunction` | Discourse markers | both | Contrasting conjunctions | substrings: but, however, instead, although, even though, despite, and yet, nevertheless, nonetheless | same | "That's nice but it's unnecessary" |
| 17 | `Reassurance` | Agreement & stance | both | Minimizing the other's problems | phrases: is okay, not worry, no big deal, not a big deal, no problem, no worries, is fine, you are good | same | "Don't worry, we're still on track" |
| 18 | `Ask.Agency` | Requests & agency | both | Requesting an action for oneself | phrases: do me a favor, let me, allow me, can i, should i, may i, might i, could i | same | "Let me step back for a minute" |
| 19 | `Give.Agency` | Requests & agency | both | Suggesting an action for the other | phrases: let you, allow you, you can, you may, you could | same | "I want to let you come out ahead" |
| 20 | `Hello` | Greetings & closings | both | Greetings | words hi, hello, hey, greetings, howdy + phrases good morning/evening/afternoon | same | "Hi, how are you today?" |
| 21 | `Please` | Requests & agency | both | Expressing 'please' | word: please | same | "Let me know if that works, please" |
| 22 | `First.Person.Plural` | Pronouns & address | both | First-person plural pronouns | words: we, us, our, ours, ourselves | same | "It's a good deal for both of us" |
| 23 | `First.Person.Single` | Pronouns & address | both | First-person singular pronouns | words: i, me, my, mine, myself | same | "It would benefit me, as well" |
| 24 | `Second.Person` | Pronouns & address | both | Second-person pronouns | words: you, your, yours, yourself, yourselves | same | "It would benefit you, as well" |
| 25 | `Third.Person` | Pronouns & address | both | Third-person pronouns | words: he, him, his, himself, she, her, hers, herself, they, them, their, theirs, themselves | same | "They are out of their minds" |
| 26 | `Questions` | Questions | none only | Number of question marks | count of '?' in the raw text | (replaced by the four question types) | "Is this for real?" |
| 27 | `Positive.Emotion` | Emotion & sentiment | both (rule differs) | Positive emotion words | words from a 2,006-word positive list | positive words outside a negation window + negative words inside one ('not bad') | "That is a great deal" |
| 28 | `Negative.Emotion` | Emotion & sentiment | both (rule differs) | Negative emotion words | words from a 4,783-word negative list | negative words outside a negation window + positive words inside one ('not good') | "That is a bad deal" |
| 29 | `Agreement` | Agreement & stance | spacy only | Explicit statement of agreement | - | un-negated parses nsubj(agree\|concur, i\|we), acomp(are\|is, right\|correct\|true) + {good, great, excellent, brilliant, fair, amazing} {idea, point, suggestion} | "I mostly agree with that" |
| 30 | `Disagreement` | Agreement & stance | spacy only | Explicit disagreement | - | negated agreement or nsubj(think\|believe, i\|we); un-negated nsubj(disagree\|object, i\|we), acomp(..., wrong\|incorrect\|false\|untrue), a lie / a myth; {bad, terrible, horrible, awful, dumb, stupid} {idea, point, suggestion} | "I don't agree with that" |
| 31 | `Acknowledgement` | Agreement & stance | spacy only | Explicit statement of understanding | - | un-negated nsubj(understand\|see\|acknowledge\|hear\|get, i\|we), dobj(take, point) | "I understand your point" |
| 32 | `Subjectivity` | Hedging & certainty | spacy only | Identifying a personal perspective | - | nsubj(think\|believe\|suspect\|thought\|felt\|presume\|reckon\|feel, i\|we), poss(perspective\|belief\|view\|knowledge\|opinion, my\|our) | "I think that is fair" |
| 33 | `Bare.Command` | Requests & agency | spacy only | Unconjugated verb starting a sentence | - | sentence-initial token tagged VB, except be, do, have, hope, excuse, thank, please, hang, let | "Lower the price for me" |
| 34 | `WH.Questions` | Questions | spacy only | Questions with a WH word (who, what, where, when, why, how, which) | - | question sentences with a WH word before the root verb | "Why did you settle on that value?" |
| 35 | `Repair.Questions` | Questions | spacy only | Requests for repetition/clarification | - | who?, what?, pardon?, sorry?, huh?, hm? (punct relation to '?') | "Sorry?" |
| 36 | `Tag.Questions` | Questions | spacy only | Tag questions | - | right? / you know? / eh? / do you? / don't you? in the raw text | "That's fair, right?" |
| 37 | `YesNo.Questions` | Questions | spacy only | Questions without a WH word | - | Questions - WH - Repair - Tag (clipped at 0) | "Is this for real?" |
| 38 | `Gratitude` | Gratitude & apology | both (rule differs) | Expressions of thanks | words starting with thank / grateful / gratitude | same + un-negated '(appreciate, i)' / '(appreciate, we)' | "Thanks for your interest" |
| 39 | `Apology` | Gratitude & apology | both (rule differs) | Apologies ('sorry', 'oops', 'excuse me', ...) | words: sorry, oops, whoops, apologize | un-negated: oops/woops/whoops, I am sorry, sorry (as root), I/we apologize/regret, excuse me, forgive me, your forgiveness, we are sorry, I want/have/need/would like to apologize, say sorry | "I'm sorry for being so blunt" |
| 40 | `Truth.Intensifier` | Hedging & certainty | both (rule differs) | Indicators of certainty | words really, actually, honestly, surely + phrase 'in fact' | same words + the point / the reality / the truth / in fact (parse) | "This is actually a good idea." |
| 41 | `Adverb.Limiter` | Hedging & certainty | spacy only | Minimizing with just / only / merely / simply | - | advmod relation to just, only, merely, simply | "It is just enough to be worth it" |
| 42 | `Affirmation` | Agreement & stance | both | Short affirmation at the start | first word of the text is yeah, yes, ok, okay, perfect, fine, wow, great, amazing | same | "Okay, that will work out then" |
| 43 | `Conjunction.Start` | Discourse markers | both | Begins with a conjunction | first word of the text is so, then, and, but, or, however | same | "And if that works for you" |

Column order with `parser="none"`: `Hedges`, `Impersonal.Pronoun`, `Swearing`, `Negation`, `Filler.Pause`, `Informal.Title`, `Formal.Title`, `Could.You`, `Can.You`, `By.The.Way`, `Let.Me.Know`, `Goodbye`, `For.Me`, `For.You`, `Reasoning`, `Contrast.Conjunction`, `Reassurance`, `Ask.Agency`, `Give.Agency`, `Hello`, `Please`, `First.Person.Plural`, `First.Person.Single`, `Second.Person`, `Third.Person`, `Questions`, `Positive.Emotion`, `Negative.Emotion`, `Gratitude`, `Apology`, `Truth.Intensifier`, `Affirmation`, `Conjunction.Start`.

Column order with `parser="spacy"`: `Hedges`, `Impersonal.Pronoun`, `Swearing`, `Negation`, `Filler.Pause`, `Informal.Title`, `Formal.Title`, `Could.You`, `Can.You`, `By.The.Way`, `Let.Me.Know`, `Goodbye`, `For.Me`, `For.You`, `Reasoning`, `Contrast.Conjunction`, `Reassurance`, `Ask.Agency`, `Give.Agency`, `Hello`, `Please`, `First.Person.Plural`, `First.Person.Single`, `Second.Person`, `Third.Person`, `Positive.Emotion`, `Negative.Emotion`, `Agreement`, `Disagreement`, `Acknowledgement`, `Subjectivity`, `Bare.Command`, `WH.Questions`, `Repair.Questions`, `Tag.Questions`, `YesNo.Questions`, `Gratitude`, `Apology`, `Truth.Intensifier`, `Adverb.Limiter`, `Affirmation`, `Conjunction.Start`.

Categories: Agreement & stance, Discourse markers, Emotion & sentiment, Gratitude & apology, Greetings & closings, Hedging & certainty, Lexical, Pronouns & address, Questions, Requests & agency.

## 2. `politenessDNM()` columns

The 20 original features of Danescu-Niculescu-Mizil et al. (2013), counts per
text (always computed with spaCy). "Start" means the first token of a sentence.

| # | column | how it is counted | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `Counterfactual.Modal` | could you / would you / might you | "Could you help?" |
| 2 | `Indicative.Modal` | can you / will you | "Can you help?" |
| 3 | `First.Person.Plural` | we, our, ours, us, ourselves | "We can do it" |
| 4 | `Indirect.Start` | 'by the way' | "By the way, ..." |
| 5 | `Direct.Start` | sentence starts with so / then / and / but / or | "So what now?" |
| 6 | `Factuality` | really, actually, honestly, surely + the point/reality/truth, in fact | "In fact, it works" |
| 7 | `Apologizing` | woops, oops, sorry + I apologize, excuse me, forgive me | "Sorry about that" |
| 8 | `Affirmation` | sentence starts with great, good, nice, interesting, cool, excellent, awesome | "Great, thanks" |
| 9 | `Gratitude` | words starting with 'thank' + I appreciate | "Thank you" |
| 10 | `Greeting` | hi, hello, hey | "Hello there" |
| 11 | `Direct.Questions` | who / what / why / how as the 1st or 2nd token of a sentence | "Why is that?" |
| 12 | `Positive.Emotion` | positive words (no negation scoping) | "Great deal" |
| 13 | `Negative.Emotion` | negative words (no negation scoping) | "Bad deal" |
| 14 | `Hedges` | older, larger hedge list (incl. think, feel, ...), counted as substrings | "I think so" |
| 15 | `Please.Start` | sentence starts with 'please' | "Please help" |
| 16 | `First.Person.Single.Start` | sentence starts with i / me / my / mine / myself | "I agree" |
| 17 | `Second.Person.Start` | sentence starts with you / your / yours / yourself / yourselves | "You are right" |
| 18 | `Please` | 'please' not at the start of a sentence | "Help, please" |
| 19 | `First.Person.Single` | i / me / my / mine / myself not at the start of a sentence | "That is my offer" |
| 20 | `Second.Person` | you / your / ... not at the start of a sentence | "Thank you" |

## 3. Other functions

| function | returns |
|---|---|
| `receptiveness(texts)` | NumPy array, one conversational-receptiveness score per text (pre-trained linear model on 16 politeness features; higher = more receptive to opposing views; on the scale of the training ratings, which range from about −3.8 to 2.7, 90% between −1.8 and 1.5) |
| `politenessModel(texts)` | NumPy array, one politeness score per text (LASSO trained on the DNM et al. 2013 annotations; higher = more polite; refitted on each call, so it varies slightly unless `random_state`/`foldid` is fixed) |
| `trainModel(train, covar, test)` | dict: `train_proj` (in-sample predictions at lambda.min; probabilities if `covar` is binary), `test_proj` (predictions for `test` at lambda.1se, or `None`), `train_coefs` (pandas Series of non-zero coefficients), `train_model` (`CVGlmnet`: `.lambda_`, `.cvm`, `.cvsd`, `.lambda_min`, `.lambda_1se`, `.coef(s)`, `.predict(x, s, type)`) |
| `featurePlot(df, split, ...)` | matplotlib `Figure` (`fig.polite_data` = plotted data) |
| `featurePlotData(df, split, ...)` | dict: `data` (DataFrame: `feature`, `count` = group mean, `cond` = group, `se`, `count_minus`/`count_plus` = CI bounds), `map_type` (axis title), `y_breaks`, `y_labels`, `y_trans`, `split_levels`, `split_cols` |
| `modelPlot(model, counts, dat=False)` | matplotlib `Figure`, or dict `plot`/`data` with `dat=True` |
| `modelPlotData(model, counts)` | DataFrame: `feat`, `score` (coefficient), `freq` (mean uses per document), rounded to 3 decimals |
| `exampleTexts(text, covar, type, num_docs)` | list of the `num_docs` texts with the highest (`"most"`) or lowest (`"least"`) covariate |
| `describe(df)` | DataFrame per column: `description`, `mean`, `share_of_texts` (> 0), `max` |
| `slogodds(x, y)` | dict `lor` (log odds ratio), `slor` (variance-weighted) |
| `getTokenSets(text, parser)` | dict of intermediate token sets (`clean`, `c.words`, `dicts`, and with spaCy `p.nonum`, `p.negs`, ...; see HOW_IT_WORKS.md §2.6) |
| `datasets.*()` | example data from the R package: `phone_offers`, `bowl_offers`, `receptive_train`, `receptive_polite`, `polite_train`, `feature_table`, `receptive_names`, word lists |
